questions.q: What does the summary say people usually need when something goes wrong in their life?
a: Someone to listen and feel the situation alongside them
A clear plan for fixing the problem step by step
Honest criticism about what they did to cause it
Quiet time alone to work through it by themselves
questions.why: Lesson 1 says advice rarely helps; most people need someone to empathize with them.

questions.q: Why does the summary compare parenting to a jigsaw puzzle missing its last piece?
a: Children need to work some things out on their own to grow
Parents should hide the hardest pieces until kids are older
Every family problem has exactly one correct solution
Children give up quickly when a task becomes frustrating
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the puzzle to show that solving everything for children blocks their progress.

questions.q: What does Kelly Corrigan claim about refusing requests in a relationship?
a: It is vital, and the person who says it deserves respect
It should be avoided because it always sounds selfish
It is acceptable only between very close friends
It works best when it comes with an apology afterward
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues that saying no is essential to healthy relationships, not a sign of laziness.

questions.q: How did Kelly react when her husband said he did not want to pursue more children?
a: She accepted it so they could move forward together
She kept pushing until he finally changed his mind
She began adoption proceedings without telling him
She asked her father to talk him out of it
questions.why: Lesson 2 shows Kelly choosing to stay together, even though it meant giving up her dream.

questions.q: What did Kelly’s father mean when he said she would eventually work things out?
a: A few victories now and then are enough to keep you going
Perfection is reachable if you simply try hard enough
Everyone finds success at roughly the same age
You should measure your progress against your friends
questions.why: Lesson 3 closes with his point that nobody needs to be perfect every day.
